account: RL-Zero-Math changes the base by 0.24 % of its weight norm, with 12 % of that change in 8 paired input-output directions per matrix that lie in the base's own most-driven activation directions; any on-policy RL reward concentrates this way (LM-judge General-RL top-8 share 0.127, Math 0.135, imitation-only Think-SFT 0.030) because the update only re-weights text the base already writes, and those 8 pairs at 1.5x alone match RL (456 vs 457 of 500 on MATH-500, 200.25 vs 200.0 on hard328) while random, unpaired or Think-SFT directions of equal norm do nothing.

The re-weighting does two things to the base's token habits: it opens the answer in deliberation mode ('Okay', 'Wait'), which RL learns mostly in its first 100 steps (step 100 plain 418 vs cued base 410, same cap-hit rate), and it then lowers the per-step slip rate and lets a finished derivation wrap up (step 100 to final +45 of 500, cap hits -2.9 points, RL half as likely as the base to write the base's own wrong step).

The opening is fully available at inference: a three-token cue (224 to 410 of 500), a self-opened draw (411) or a one-tensor hand edit that writes the cue (397) gives it with no RL weights, which is why the cue alone reaches 78 % of RL's MATH-500 gain and the same Math cue works on code and on general questions.

The slip part is available only by resampling, and resampling works because the base's slips are independent one-off events, not shared attractors (same-problem wrong-pair agreement 0.26 vs 0.005 by chance; merging the wrong answers costs a 4-vote 0.07): where chains are short the base already writes the right answer in some samples (81 % of RL's MATH-500 gain on problems it solves at least 1 in 4; 75 % of Code-edit fixes passed in another base sample, the edit keeping base passes only at a base resample's rate), so a vote over about 6 base samples matches one RL sample.

Because a lower slip rate compounds over chain length, on long hard328 derivations RL's extra right answers fall where the base has no right sample in 4 (26 of 36 vote wins), and neither more tokens nor restarts buy them, since the base's long answers are loops at T 0.6 (52 %) or unsolved cap hits at T 1.0 (+1.2 points at a 32k cap), so inference stops 8.8 points [5.5, 12.5] short of RL there.

The pairs act per domain on what the reward paid for, not by how strongly a text drives their inputs: Math's directions, driven 87 % as much by code text as by math, add only +1.5 points to code pass rate against Code's +7.0 and neither box code nor drop its block, and answer-format habits (no box, no fence) sit on problems of average difficulty, not on failures to solve.

consequences.claim: On hard328 the cued base's finished wrong answers also scatter, so the vote over its 4 samples with the real wrong answers is right clearly more often than the same vote with every finished wrong answer of a problem merged into one value. S4 says vote gains come from independent one-off slips, so D lies in [0.06, 0.40]; if hard-problem wrongs shared one attractor, D would be about 0.
consequences.why_new: F37 measured this on MATH-500 with 12 samples; F23/F42 measured MATH-500 agreement only. No fact or result gives the merged-wrong vote contrast on hard328, where wrong answers could plausibly concentrate on shared traps.
consequences.statistic: D = mean over problems of P(vote of 4 right | real answers) - P(vote of 4 right | finished wrong answers merged), in probability units
consequences.rows: hard328 problems whose 4 attempt-0 samples (samples 0-3, no restarts) hold at least 1 right and at least 1 finished wrong answer under grader v3; cap-hit samples abstain
consequences.computation: 1) Read attempt 0 of samples 0-3 per problem; label right, finished wrong (with its extracted answer) or cap hit. 2) Keep problems with >=1 right and >=1 finished wrong. 3) Real vote: plurality over finished answers, ties broken evenly (expected value of a random tie break). 4) Merged vote: replace every finished wrong value of the problem by one token, vote again the same way. 5) D = mean(real - merged). 6) 90 % interval: 10,000 bootstrap resamples of problems, 5th and 95th percentiles.
consequences.null: Merged-wrong vote (the base's wrong answers on a problem share one attractor value), where D = 0 exactly; the strongest null for this statistic.

consequences.claim: RL step 100 has learned only the opening (S2), not the lower slip rate, so its wrong answers scatter like the cued base's and a vote over its 4 samples gains as much over one sample as the cued base's vote does (+7.1 points), not as little as final RL's (+2.8).
consequences.why_new: F07/F38 and result-6832a8 give step 100's single-sample score and cap hits only; no fact or result computes a vote over step-100 samples.
consequences.statistic: Vote-over-4 right minus mean single-sample right for RL step 100 plain, in points of 500 (percentage points)
consequences.rows: all 500 MATH-500 problems, the 4 step-100 plain samples (sample 0 from s0100_plain-01, samples 1-3 from s0100_plain_s123-01), T 1.0, grader v3
consequences.computation: 1) Per problem, the 4 samples' extracted answers and v3 grades. 2) Vote: plurality over finished answers, ties broken evenly (expected value). 3) Single: mean right of the 4 samples. 4) G = 100 * mean over problems (vote right - single right). 5) 90 % interval: 10,000 bootstrap resamples of problems.
consequences.null: Final RL's own vote gain (results/day1_3/math500_rl-01: vote 474 vs mean single 460, +2.8 points), i.e. step 100 already carrying RL's lowered slip rate.

consequences.claim: The 1.5x top-8 edit is a weight change that lowers the slip rate the way RL does (S1, S2, S5), so on hard328 problems where the cued base has no right answer in 4 samples it is right per sample as often as RL plain: the edit-minus-RL rate lies in [-0.08, 0.08]. If the edit were only a resample of the base, it would sit near the base's own rate there and about 0.2 below RL.
consequences.why_new: result-95a4dc matches edit and RL on totals; F04/F26 split by one base sample's outcome. No fact or result compares edit and RL on the problems outside the base's 4-sample reach.
consequences.statistic: Edit per-sample right rate minus RL plain per-sample right rate on base-0-of-4 hard328 problems, in probability units
consequences.rows: hard328 problems with 0 right among the cued base's attempt-0 samples 0-3; for each, the edit's 4 samples and RL plain's 4 attempt-0 samples
consequences.computation: 1) Select problems with 0 of 4 right for the cued base (attempt 0). 2) Per problem, edit rate = right of the edit's 4 samples / 4; RL rate = right of RL's 4 attempt-0 samples / 4. 3) D = mean over problems (edit - RL). 4) 90 % interval: 10,000 bootstrap resamples of problems. 5) Null value on the same rows: base cue rate from the base's restart attempts and the independent 32k-cap base cue run scored at 16,384 (results/cap32/base_cue-01) minus the RL rate.
consequences.null: The edit as a base resample: its rate on these problems equals the cued base's own fresh-sample rate (near 0.05), giving D about -0.2.
